MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A cuboid is 8 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 5 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 15 blocks
   B. 80 blocks
   C. 16 blocks
   D. 88 blocks

2. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 35 blocks
   B. 28 blocks
   C. 30 blocks
   D. 10 blocks

3. What is the total value of the digit 1 in 1,523? (1 mark)
   A. 100
   B. 10,000
   C. 1,000
   D. 1

4. Which sum checks that 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225? (1 mark)
   A. 8,500 + 5,225
   B. 8,500 + 3,275
   C. 5,225 − 3,275
   D. 5,225 + 3,275

5. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 50 cm
   B. 2 m 50 cm
   C. 3 m
   D. 25 cm

6. Write 6/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 6.0
   B. 0.06
   C. 0.6
   D. 0.006

7. A bottle top is usually tightened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. clockwise
   B. anticlockwise
   C. sideways
   D. up and down

8. The price Ksh 12.50 shows how many whole shillings and how many cents? (1 mark)
   A. 1 shilling and 250 cents
   B. 12 shillings and 50 cents
   C. 125 shillings and no cents
   D. 12 shillings and 5 cents

9. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 9 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 6:45
   B. 9:30
   C. 10:30
   D. 9:06

10. In the number 0.74, the digit 4 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundredths
   B. Tens
   C. Ones
   D. Tenths

11. Change 135 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 15 min
   B. 2 h 45 min
   C. 1 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 15 min

12. Which sum checks that 6,003 − 2,475 = 3,528? (1 mark)
   A. 3,528 − 2,475
   B. 3,528 + 2,475
   C. 6,003 + 2,475
   D. 6,003 + 3,528

13. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. How many litres do 100 jerrycans hold? (1 mark)
   A. 1,990 litres
   B. 2,000 litres
   C. 2,100 litres
   D. 1,980 litres

14. A fence uses 5 pieces of wire, each 3 m 50 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 18 m 50 cm
   B. 17 m 50 cm
   C. 17 m 40 cm
   D. 3 m 55 cm

15. Which of these is a factor of 24? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 8
   C. 5
   D. 7

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. A tank holds 20 L of water. In the morning 4 1/2 L is taken out and in the afternoon 3 3/4 L is taken out. How much water is left in the tank? (5 marks)

17. Using the vehicle data (5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses, 1 lorry), which type was seen most and how many more matatus than buses were seen? (3 marks)

18. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks and cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Work out both volumes and say which is greater. (4 marks)

19. A bus leaves at 10:30 a.m. and arrives at 2:15 p.m. How long is the journey? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 80 blocks
   One layer has 8 × 2 = 16 blocks. There are 5 layers, so the volume is 16 × 5 = 80 blocks.

2. C — 30 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 2 = 10 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 10 × 3 = 30 blocks.

3. C — 1,000
   The digit 1 is in the thousands place, so its total value is 1 × 1,000 = 1,000.

4. D — 5,225 + 3,275
   Addition undoes subtraction. 5,225 + 3,275 = 8,500, the starting number.

5. B — 2 m 50 cm
   250 ÷ 100 = 2 remainder 50. So 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm.

6. B — 0.06
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 6/100 = 0.06.

7. A — clockwise
   Tightening a bottle top means turning it clockwise.

8. B — 12 shillings and 50 cents
   The digits after the decimal point show the cents.

9. B — 9:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 9:30.

10. A — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 0.74 the digit 4 is in the hundredths place.

11. A — 2 h 15 min
   135 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 15, so 135 minutes = 2 h 15 min.

12. B — 3,528 + 2,475
   Addition undoes subtraction. 3,528 + 2,475 = 6,003, the starting number.

13. B — 2,000 litres
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 2,000 litres.

14. B — 17 m 50 cm
   350 × 5 = 1750 cm = 17 m 50 cm.

15. B — 8
   24 ÷ 8 = 3 with nothing left over, so 8 is a factor of 24. The others leave a remainder.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: 11 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Total taken: 4 1/2 + 3 3/4 = 4 2/4 + 3 3/4 = 7 5/4 = 8 1/4 L (3 marks). 20 − 8 1/4 = 11 3/4 L (2 marks).

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Matatus. 5 − 2 = 3 more matatus than buses.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for matatu, 1 mark for 5 − 2, 1 mark for 3.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: A = 40 blocks, B = 60 blocks. B is greater by 20 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for the volumes, 1 mark for the comparison, 1 mark for the difference.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 2 h (1 mark); 12:30 to 2:15 p.m. is 1 h 45 min (1 mark); total 3 h 45 min (1 mark).
